BlockMIPTest.pins: MIPs of large-file results from the blocks their tasks write: MIP_zarr_block_mips (with range_max_3d_mex), MIP_zarr_save_block_mips and MIP_zarr_merge_block_mips, which XR_MIP_zarr uses to make the same MIP slabs and MIPs it computes from the zarr, and MIP_zarr_batch_size

batchSizeGrowsForSlabsOver100GB.pins: the batch grows by a block along the axis of the largest slab until no slab is over 100 GiB (3 steps here), or the batch is (21 steps, to a 104 GiB batch); values of XR_MIP_zarr before the batch size moved to MIP_zarr_batch_size

batchSizeIsRoundedToBlocksAndCapped.pins: batch size is rounded to blocks and capped

blockMIPsAreCastAsTheZarrStoresThem.pins: single blocks written to a uint16 zarr (large-file decon with save16bit) are rounded and saturated as written

blockMIPsWithoutTheMexMatch.pins: platforms without range_max_3d_mex take the max of each part

flagIsMovedIntoPlace.pins: the flag marks the task as done, so it must not be seen half written

mergeKeepsToTheMemoryLimit.pins: the y slab and its coverage count (5 x 29 x 23 x 3 bytes) and the blocks' MIPs (blocks overlap 10 batches along y in all: 10 x 29 x 23 x 2 bytes) are 23345 bytes, 2.174e-5 GiB

mergeNeedsBlocksThatCoverTheImageOnce.pins: two overlapping blocks and a gap of the same size add up to the image size

mergeNeedsMIPsOfAllBlocks.pins: flags of tasks without MIPs (older code), MIPs for other batches, or blocks that don't cover the image give no slab, so that the caller reads the image

mergedSlabsMatchTheImage.pins: blocks not aligned with the MIP batches, written by tasks in an order that isn't their order in the image; for single, a region of NaN and of -0 and 0, where max takes the first value

rangeMaxMatchesMaxOfEachRange.pins: range max matches max of each range

xrMIPZarrMergesTheBlockMIPs.pins: the same slab zarrs (data, chunks, data type) and MIPs as from the zarr, without job framework tasks

xrMIPZarrReadsTheZarrIfAFlagHasNoMIPs.pins: all or nothing: the other flags' MIPs are wrong here, so a partial merge would show

xrMIPZarrReadsTheZarrWithoutMemoryForThe.pins: the flags' MIPs are wrong here, so a merge would show

xrMIPZarrResumesFromExistingSlabs.pins: slab zarrs from an earlier run are used for missing MIPs, as before (the flags' MIPs are wrong here)

ComputingMemoryEstimateTest.pins: XR_estimateComputingMemory: memory (GB) for each processing step of an image, rawImageSize * memFactors(step) (deskew: also times (nz / 300) ^ 2 above 300 slices), and the GPU memory of deconvolution

dataSizeWithSeveralSteps.pins: with dataSize, several steps failed at || (a condition of two values)

eachStepOfSeveralGetsItsEstimate.pins: a step was estimated only if every step matched it, so with the default three steps every estimate was 0 and the GPU estimate was not assigned

singleStepsAsTheCallersPassThem.pins: the callers pass one step: their estimates stay as they were

FixedOrderStatTest.pins: fixed_order_stat: MATLAB's sum, mean, var and std of all elements in its order at one thread, bit for bit (also -0), at any number of threads (here 1, 2, 4 and 24). MATLAB splits sums of 89000 or more elements among its threads, so its own results there change in the last bits with the thread count (in 778 to 821 of 1476 cases of a probe on Linux at 2 to 24 threads); below 89000 elements, and f...

callersAskForMatlabsExpressions.pins: the registration's NCC, the crop of its region and decon's debug error metric take MATLAB's expressions of before (mean(T(:), 'double'), ..., var(A(:), 1)) from fixed_order_stat: a spy records its calls and returns MATLAB's own value; at one thread their results are the same as with fixed_order_stat (on Linux, where its order is MATLAB's)

isMatlabsAtOneThread.pins: around MATLAB's switches (44 elements: lanes, 89000: blocks of 4096), with a last block that isn't full and a last group of four lanes that isn't either, and a volume: from 89000 elements the same at every thread count, on Linux MATLAB's order at one thread (as found for R2024b); below, MATLAB's own sums, which don't depend on the thread count on Linux and macOS (as measured)

otherArraysAndOptionsAreMatlabs.pins: integer (exact in double), logical and complex data, options it doesn't take: MATLAB's own function of x(:)

signedZerosAndNonFiniteValues.pins: a sum of -0s is -0 (also the mean), a +0 among them +0; NaN and Inf give NaN or Inf as in MATLAB (above 89000 elements)

MIPTest.pins: maximum intensity projections: XR_MIP_wrapper (tiff, zarr and large zarr paths), saveMIP_tiff, and max_pooling_3d; and min_bbox_3d

allAxesOfLargeZarr.pins: batch-wise MIPs of a zarr file, merged across batches

inputBboxProjectsTheCroppedRegion.pins: input bbox projects the cropped region

largeZarrInputBboxThatEndsBeforeTheImage.pins: (XR_MIP_zarr) the last batches of a box whose size isn't a multiple of the batch size ran to the end of the image instead of the box, so their MIPs went past the end of the MIP slabs and writezarr raised "Upper bound is invalid"

largeZarrJobsAskForWhatTheyHold.pins: the job of a large file (XR_MIP_zarr) runs its MIP batches as jobs (1 CPU each). It asked for 16 B per voxel of the whole input: whole nodes for large data. Now it asks for MATLAB with one CPU, and if it computes batches itself (masterCompute, the config's if it sets it), for cpusPerTask (default 3) and a batch's estimate (2048^3 uint16, 64 GB in MATLAB jobs). The input is a 34 G-voxel header (...

largeZarrJobsGoAfterTheirBatches.pins: the job of a large file waits for its MIP batch jobs: it asks to go after them (nice, coordinator_nice); the jobs of other files don't (the framework is a spy)

maxPoolingOfNegativeValues.pins: KNOWN ISSUE (may be intended): max_pooling_3d_mex initializes each block maximum with 0, so blocks with only negative values return 0 instead of their maximum. The MATLAB fallback (max_pooling_3d.m) zero-pads edge blocks, so it does the same there. Non-negative input may be an intended precondition (the mex has no signed integer types, and stitching treats 0 as no data); if not, initialize with...

minimumOfARegion.pins: min_bbox_3d: the minimum of a region, by min_bbox_3d_mex (Linux only) or by the MATLAB code (elsewhere, for int16, or where the mex fails), which returned the minimum along y instead

minimumOfARegionSkipsNaN.pins: as the mex: NaN is skipped, and a region of NaN only or without voxels gives the largest value of the class

mipsAreMovedIntoPlace.pins: XR_MIP_wrapper's tasks count as done once their MIPs exist, so a MIP written in place could be seen, and its job cancelled, while half written

slabAnotherWriterMadeIsKept.pins: a MIP slab that another writer (of the same result) had put in place was deleted and replaced; it is kept, and the MIP of its axis is made from it

zarrIsReadInSlabsOfWholeChunks.pins: saveMIP_zarr reads zarr files in z slabs of whole chunk layers with at least 64 chunks (3 slabs of one layer here, 2 slabs of two layers in the box) and keeps a running max along z. For single, lines of NaN and of -0 and 0, where max takes the first (0 first in the second and third slab here).

ParallelRsyncWrapperTest.pins: XR_parallel_rsync_wrapper, which copies a folder in batches of rsync calls run by the job framework (a spy here), then with one rsync of the whole folder

batchScriptIsFoundWhicheverSetupIsFirst.pins: the wrapper found the code by the first setup.m on the path and a folder named PetaKit5D: with another setup.m first (e.g., of an app that bundles PetaKit5D), or with the code in a folder of another name, it changed to a folder that doesn't exist, or gave the jobs a batch script that doesn't exist

clusterFileCheckFindsTheFiles.pins: batch_file_exist_cluster (the check of 100000 files or more) used undefined MatlabLaunchStr, mccMode and configFile, so it always failed

clusterFileCheckOfABatchOfOnePath.pins: the task of a batch of one path (e.g., the last batch of 50001 files) wrote no result, so its check never finished

eachBatchIsCheckedByItsLastFile.pins: the job framework counts a batch as done once its checked file exists, and cancels the remaining jobs when all are; the second to last file of each batch was checked, so the last one could be cut short, and a last batch of fewer files had none

failedClusterFileChecksAreCheckedHere.pins: a batch whose check failed in its jobs (here every batch: a framework spy that runs nothing) made the result a cell of empties, on which the rsync wrapper failed; such batches are checked in this MATLAB, with a warning

largeCopiesPassTheirSettingsToTheCluster.pins: copies of 100000 files or more are checked by jobs: the wrapper's settings go to the check (a stub here, given 100000 file names that report all files as copied)

namesWithSpacesCommasAndQuotesAreCopied.pins: paths had their spaces escaped as '\ ' (also in the checked files, so files with spaces were never found, and a batch checked by one was skipped), the batch script split its lists at commas (a name with a comma), and the final rsync had its paths unquoted (a folder with a space)

ResampleTest.pins: XR_resample_dataset / XR_resampleFrame / XR_resampleSingleZarr. resampleFactor is in yxz order; a factor of 2 downsamples 2x.

image2dWithYxzFactor.pins: 2D images used to be resampled with the x and z factors of a yxz factor

imresize3FastMatchesImresize3.pins: imresize3_fast replaces imresize3 in the resampling; imresize3 is replaced by a spy that errors when called with an output, so the result comes from the fast path, not from the fallback

imresize3FastRegionMatchesCroppedImresiz.pins: with an output region, imresize3_fast resizes only the input region it depends on (in outClass if given): the same values as the region of imresize3's result (the whole output, a corner, the far end, the middle voxel)

imresize3FastRegionWithOtherMethods.pins: methods other than linear and cubic crop imresize3's result

inputBboxResamplesTheCroppedRegion.pins: input bbox resamples the cropped region

largeZarrKeepsResultOfAnotherCopy.pins: two copies of a task (e.g. a retry next to a slow first try) share the temporary result; the copy that finished second deleted the result the first one had moved into place

largeZarrKeepsResultOfAnotherRun.pins: a copy from another run (its own uuid) that finds the result published replaced it with its own, incomplete result

largeZarrMatchesInMemory.pins: batch-wise resampling with border buffers vs the whole image. The border is a multiple of the factor, see the known issue largeZarrWithDefaultBorderSize.

largeZarrWithDefaultBorderSize.pins: batches used to be shifted by half an output voxel when the border (default [5, 5, 5]) is not a multiple of the factor

maxAndMeanMatchBlockReference.pins: non-divisible size: edge blocks use only the voxels inside

SystemMemoryTest.pins: getSystemMemory, which stitching uses to choose how to make the MIP of the result

memoryIsNotTheValueOfAParentJob.pins: a job submitted from another job (as the jobs of a job that coordinates jobs are) inherits the other's SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE (a 32-CPU controller got 16 GB, its master's): the memory is the limit of the job's own cgroup. In a Slurm job only: the job of the tests, from its cgroup (pktest.NoSlurmFixture hides its variables)

memoryPerNodeNextToMemoryPerCPUIsNotTake.pins: without the job's cgroup (here a job id that isn't this process's), SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE next to SLURM_MEM_PER_CPU is one job's value in another's environment, so scontrol tells (it knows no job 123: unknown)

slurmJobMemoryIsInGB.pins: in a job started with --mem, the memory was returned as the text of SLURM_MEM_PER_NODE (MB)

TiffZarrConversionTest.pins: tiff <-> zarr conversion (XR_tiffToZarr_wrapper, XR_zarrToTiff_wrapper, tiffToZarr, zarrToTiff) and zarr resaving (XR_resave_zarr_wrapper). XR_zarrToTiff_wrapper doesn't forward parseCluster to the job framework, so on a machine with Slurm it submits jobs; the shared pktest.NoSlurmFixture keeps it local.

resaveGroupedBatchesDoNotTakeOtherFlags.pins: a run that groups batches, with the uuid of an interrupted run that wrote one batch at a time (and finished its first task, batches 1-5), must not take that task's flag for its own first task (groups 1-5)

resaveGroupedBatchesWriteTheSameChunks.pins: batches read and written together give the same chunk files as one batch at a time (cpp-zarr writes deterministic chunks), also with a crop and batches of two chunks that don't divide the image

resaveGroupsBatchesWithoutCluster.pins: without a cluster, neighboring batches are read and written together (along y, then x and z, up to one chunk per thread), so that cpp-zarr compresses their chunks in parallel (writes of one chunk at a time kept a few cores busy); cluster tasks, and too little or unknown memory, keep one batch per read and write

resaveGroupsWithinTheShareOfTheMemory.pins: the batches read and written together take at most 1/16 of this process's share of the memory: the memory times its share of the CPUs (a local process pool divides the threads among its workers), so that processes that resave at once stay within it

resaveKeepsResultOfAnotherCopy.pins: two copies of a task (e.g. a retry next to a slow first try) share the temporary result; the copy that finished second deleted the result the first one had moved into place

resaveKeepsResultOfAnotherRun.pins: a copy from another run (its own uuid) that finds the result published replaced it with its own, incomplete result

resaveOnLocalPoolGroupsWithinTheWorkersT.pins: files resaved on a local process pool (localWorkerNum in the configuration file): each worker has its share of the threads, and groups no more batches than that

tiffToZarrFromMemory.pins: the optional third input converts data that is already loaded

tiffToZarrPartialFilesAndFrames.pins: partial files are joined along z; an in-memory frame gets the same processing as a file; a 2D image becomes one z slice

tiffToZarrProcessingOptions.pins: flip in z, then crop (tileOutBbox), resample, and the user function, in that order; the result has the input's type

tiffToZarrReadsRegions.pins: readWholeTiff false reads the tiff by regions; without inputBbox it failed on an undefined variable (outBbox)

tiffToZarrWrapperWithInputBbox.pins: tiff to zarr wrapper with input bbox

tiffToZarrWrapperWithoutReadingWholeTiff.pins: reads the tiff in blocks with blockedImage instead of at once

tiffToZarrWritesPrivateResultInPlace.pins: with a full uuid made by the call (not on Windows, where get_uuid shortens it) no other process writes the temporary result, so its chunks are written without cpp-zarr's temporary files ('uuid' false); a given uuid can be shared by copies of a task, which keep them

zarrToTiffWrapperPassesJobSettings.pins: each task converts one file, so the memory per task is for one file (it was the sum over all files), and parseCluster, masterCompute and cpusPerTask were not passed on

UsableGPUNumTest.pins: usable_gpu_num, which counts the GPUs PetaKit5D can use and turns on forward compatibility for GPUs newer than this MATLAB supports (e.g., B200 GPUs, compute capability 10.0, which R2024b doesn't count as available without it, so GPU jobs ran on the CPU). gpuDeviceCount and gpuDevice are stubs that act as such GPUs by the real forward compatibility setting, which the tests turn off and restore,...

availableGPUsAreCountedAsTheyAre.pins: available gpus are counted as they are

forwardCompatibilityThatDoesNotHelpIsTur.pins: forward compatibility that does not help is turned off again

gpusNewerThanMATLABGetForwardCompatibili.pins: gpus newer than matlabget forward compatibility

otherFailuresLeaveForwardCompatibilityOf.pins: e.g., a GPU in use or broken: the reason is MATLAB's, and forward compatibility isn't tried (the GPUs are counted once)

WriteJsonFileTest.pins: writeJsonFile, which writes the parameters.json of every wrapper: it passed the JSON text to fprintf as the format, so a % in a value (e.g., a file name pattern like x%03d.tif) cut the file off there, and the doubled backslashes of Windows paths and of escaped characters became single ones, which made the file invalid JSON

fileHoldsTheJsonTextAsItIs.pins: file holds the json text as it is
